wils00 (0.0-5.2s): "Wilson disease is a genetic disorder where copper builds up in the liver and the brain."
wils01 (6.7-14.0s): "A mutation in the ATP7B gene stops the liver from excreting copper into bile. It's autosomal recessive."
wils02 (15.5-21.9s): "Copper damages the liver first. Then it spills into the blood, and deposits in the brain and the cornea."
wils03 (23.4-32.7s): "Children and teenagers usually present with liver disease. Young adults more often present with tremor, dystonia, slurred speech, or psychiatric change."
wils04 (34.2-42.6s): "Look at the eyes. Kayser-Fleischer rings, a brown ring at the edge of the cornea, are seen in almost all patients with brain involvement."
wils05 (44.1-50.1s): "On T2 MRI, look for symmetric bright signal in the putamen, the caudate, and the thalami."
wils06 (51.6-62.3s): "In the midbrain, the tegmentum turns bright, but the red nuclei stay dark as the eyes, and the lateral substantia nigra forms the ears. That's the face of the giant panda."
wils07 (63.8-70.0s): "On T1, the globus pallidus can be bright from liver failure, due to manganese deposition."
wils08 (71.5-80.0s): "The diagnosis rests on a low ceruloplasmin, high urinary copper, and the eye exam, with genetic testing if it's unclear."
wils09 (81.5-89.9s): "Treatment is lifelong chelation or zinc, and a liver transplant for acute liver failure. Many of the MRI changes improve with treatment."
wils10 (91.4-96.6s): "A young patient with tremor or liver disease, and a panda in the midbrain? Think Wilson disease."
Key words: Wilson; ATP7B (A-T-P seven B); autosomal recessive; dystonia (dis-TOH-nee-uh); Kayser-Fleischer (KY-zer FLY-sher); cornea; putamen (pew-TAY-men); caudate; thalami (THAL-uh-my); tegmentum (teg-MEN-tum); substantia nigra (sub-STAN-shuh NYE-gruh); globus pallidus (GLOH-bus PAL-ih-dus); manganese; ceruloplasmin (seh-ROO-loh-PLAZ-min); chelation (kee-LAY-shun)
